name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways during the scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body: In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield. Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: Each time a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" x 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Plateau, Small—A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Plateau, Small—A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" x 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: Each army’s advance has been stalled as opposing forces anchor themselves around hardened structures with only a small forest offering cover. Shatter your opponent’s defenses through traditional assault or by utilizing satchel charges to demolish their bunker and break the stalemate to seize the position.

name: Name
body: "Bunker Busters" is designed for 50- and 75-point forces.

name: Name
body: "Bunker Busters" ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: Players compete to destroy the opponent’s bunker and seize strategic territory while their opponent seeks to do the same.

name: Name
body:
Score Victory Points by damaging the opponent’s bunker, holding the forest in no man’s land, and seizing their plateau.
Hold the plateau on the opponent’s side of the table while the bunker on their side of the table is destroyed to win.

name: Name
body:
This scenario uses the map layout below. Place 2 small plateau, 1 small forest, 2 bunkers (or buildings to represent bunkers), and 4 small barriers on the table as shown on the map below. If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment with an emphasis on maintaining a relatively open field of fire for your bunkers to defend.
The plateaus and forest are terrain objectives.

name: Name
body:
At the beginning of their Maintenance Phase, a player gains Victory Points as follows:
• Hold the small forest in the center of the map with 2 or more warrior models. (1 VP)
• Hold the plateau on their opponent’s side of the table with 2 or more warrior models. (2 VPs)
Additionally, players gain Victory Points as follows. A player can only score each of these once during the game:
• Deal a total of 25 or more damage to the bunker on the opponent’s side of the table. (2 VPs)
• Destroy the bunker on the opponent’s side of the table. (2 VPs)
At the start of the game, before deployment, starting with Player 1, each player may elect a single eligible unit or solo to begin the game deployed within the bunker on their side of the table.

name: Name
body:
All warrior models are specially equipped with Satchel Charges for this mission. All warrior models gain the "Satchel Charges (★ attack)" ability.
Satchel Charges (★attack)—Target a building you are in base contact with. At the beginning of your next turn, that building suffers 4d6 points of damage.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Held at Bay— Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the beginning of your turn if your opponent’s Leader is within 12" of the rear edge of their deployment zone. 2. Secure the Perimeter— Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the end of each of your turns in which your opponent has no models on your side of the table. 3. Elite Garrison— Score 1 Victory Point once per turn when your model occupying a building destroys an enemy model.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Attrition— Score 3 Victory Points when your opponent’s last Cohort model is destroyed or removed from play. 2. Bloodletting— Score 1 Victory Point the first time one of your models damages an enemy Leader with an attack each turn. 3. Press the Attack— Score 1 Victory Point at the end of each round in which you damaged the bunker on the opponent’s side of the table and your opponent did not damage the bunker on your side of the table while that bunker is still in play.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player holding the opponent’s plateau while the opponent’s bunker is destroyed wins. Point Advantage Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with 6 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match. Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match. At the end of six rounds, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match.

name: Name
body:
"Bunker Busters" is a flexible scenario that can be easily altered to provide many different experiences. For example, players might try the following:
• Add a spike trap directly in front of each bunker and disallow the use of the "Sapper" command card.
• Replace one or both of the plateaus with Guard Towers. These will provide both pressure and protection for both your and your opponent’s bunkers while making scoring this element much more difficult.
• Make the assault on the bunkers a raid at dawn. All models gain the Stealth rule for the first 2 turns of the game.

name: Battle Forge: Bunker Busters - Chapter 1 "Bunker Busters"
